accuracy.evidence: Matches the topic's three evidence statements one to one: saying first name and age (Bo's questions, candle cakes for ages 3, 1 and 2), naming the people who live with them or look after them (three homes, then the learner's own home with mum, dad, gran, grandad, siblings, baby or a pet), and sharing one thing that is special about them (the star). Checked against Development Matters (2023), birth to three: PSED 'establish their sense of self' and 'express preferences and decisions', and Understanding the World 'make connections between the features of their family and other families', which the three different homes model. One candle per year of age is the convention the cake step uses; no claim about typical ages is made beyond the 2-3 band.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips adults see at this age and those named in the adult text: answering a different question from the one asked (each Bo question offers the age for the name and the name for the age; challenge tags agefor, namefor, homefor, likefor), counting candles past the age (cake step rejects 4 for Mia with 'Too many! Take 1 off'; challenge many and few), the belief that a family needs a mum and a dad (homes prediction, challenge needmum, m3), that small families do not count (small, m7), that pets are not part of home (pets, bigdog) and that liking something different makes someone wrong (star question, m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanics are about the self and the home: a speech-bubble conversation where only the answer that fits the question is accepted, a cake where one candle per year must match a named child's age, three houses that open to show their own families, a home the learner fills by dragging people and pets in and then reads back ('At my home: me, Mum, Gran, my cat'), and a star of special things followed by a same-or-different judgement. The distinctness gate passed against every flagship lab, including flagfeel, flaghelp and flagqw.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each idea by doing: tapping 'I am 3.' for 'What is your name?' is answered 'That tells Bo how old you are. Bo asked: What is your name?'; four candles for Mia gives 'Too many! Mia is 3, so 3 candles'; opening Leo's home reads out 'Dad, Papa, Leo, baby Kit. That is a family'; choosing 'Only me' says liking something different does not make Bo wrong. Finished tasks name the idea: one candle for each year; every family is different, and every one is a real family.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Bo asks your name. I am 3. / I am Mia.' (I am 3 is offered and corrected), 'Mia is 3. How many candles? Lots and lots / 3 candles' (adding past three is rejected), 'Mia lives with her mum and her gran. Is that a family? No, it needs a dad too / Yes' (the homes step names each home a family), and 'Bo likes blue, you like red. Is one of you wrong?' (the star step corrects Only me and Only Bo).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with rotated answer order and a streak count; twelve wrong-answer messages each name the slip, e.g. 'That is how old you are. The friend asked your name', 'Too many. One candle for each year: Sam is 2, so 2 candles', 'Families are different. Leo, his dad and his papa are a family', 'A small family is still a family', 'That is about Mum. Pick something about you', 'Pets live with us too. They can be part of home'.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short sentences of everyday words ('You have a name. When a new friend asks, say it.') and pass the family kid limit in validate_lessons; adult text passes the adult limit. Every lab screen carries one question or line, large pictures with a one-word label under each (Mum, Gran, Papa, my cat), and answers short enough for an adult to read aloud to a pre-reader.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs each carry one move: say your name, say your age with fingers and candles, who lives with you and that every home is a family, and what makes you special. Adult paragraphs give the aim, what each lab step does, named mistakes with the reason to show many kinds of family, and a puppet routine. The sorter (about me / not about me) is not a copy of any lab step.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 dark and 360 px Android light screenshots of every step plus mid-task shots (Leo's home open, Mia's cake with too many candles, the star question). Fixed two problems seen in the shots: 'Who is right?' overlapped the first answer card, so the star shrank and the answers moved to their own rows; and the red candle count on the pink cake was hard to read, so it is now dark text. Cards are 54-110 px tall with full-width button twins; nothing is clipped at 360 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: each answer to Bo, Add a candle / Take one off / That is right, a button per home, a labelled button per person or pet ('Put Gran in my home') plus 'This is my home', a button per special thing and the three answers to Bo. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action, e.g. 'Mia is 3. Candles on the cake: 4.' Challenge feedback is a polite live region with a text tick or cross; the walkthrough's axe run (WCAG 2.1 AA) was clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
